pending_commit.commit_message: lakitu: Add compute-image-packages (20160930 release) This is a part of change to add compute-image-packages (20160930 release). Compute-image-packages (20160930 release) includes three parts. This package (app-admin/compute-image-packages) installs two parts of it: google_compute_engine and google_compute_engine_init. Note that this package (app-admin/compute-image-packages) replaces app-admin/google-daemon and app-admin/google-startup-scripts in 1.3.3 release. 1) compute-image-packages-20160930.ebuild will execute setup.py (source file) to install google_compute_engine. It also installs and enables 7 systemd services from google_compute_engine_init. All of them are used for configuring google_compute_engine to run on system startup. 2) There are 6 patches that mostly come from the old package patches. However, all of them are rewrited instead of copy-and-paste because the new version of compute-image-packages (20160930 release) is very different from the old version (1.3.3 release): (1) metadata-watcher-no-infinite-loop.patch: comes from app-admin/google-startup-scripts/files/1.2.6-onboot-no-infinite-loop.patch (2) execute-startup-scripts-from-var-lib-google.patch: comes from app-admin/google-startup-scripts/files/1.2.6-execute-startup-scripts-from-var-lib-google.patch (3) set_ethtool_to_usr_sbin.patch: new patch (4) catch_read_only_root_fs.patch: new patch (5) homedir-uid-fix.patch: comes from app-admin/google-daemon/files/google-daemon-homedir-uid-fix.patch (6) do-not-block-sshd-for-google.service.patch: comes from app-admin/google-startup-scripts/files/1.2.6-do-not-block-sshd-for-google.service.patch 3) compute-image-packages-20160930.ebuild also installs and enables a special service var-lib-google-remount.service that is used for executing google-startup-scripts from /var/lib/google/. It's similar to app-admin/google-startup-scripts/files/var-lib-google-remount.service. TEST=Ran trybot and it built successfully. eCTS: Add task suite Task A wakes up B and goes to sleep. Task B wakes up C then goes to sleep. Task C wakes up A then goes to sleep. This is repeated repeat_count times: A -> B -> C -> A -> ... It's expected all tasks to run exactly repeat_count times. Tick task runs to inject some irregularity. BUG=chromium:663873 BRANCH=none TEST=cts.py -m task Change-Id: Ib7227f05f09b7a49f8528aff6e6e8d3e6df93ba7 Signed-off-by: Daisuke Nojiri <dnojiri@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/409534 Reviewed-by: Randall Spangler <rspangler@chromium.org>

eCTS: Test task priority CTS task wakes up A and C then goes to sleep: CTS -> A, C -> A -> B -> C Since C has a higher priority, C should run first. This should result in C running one more time than A (or B). BUG=chromium:663873 BRANCH=none TEST=cts.py -m task Change-Id: I89c733ba3aab09b293edf8583d6ed73791531e59 Signed-off-by: Daisuke Nojiri <dnojiri@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/409535 Reviewed-by: Randall Spangler <rspangler@chromium.org>

attestation: set key name in FinishCertRequest The caller of CreateCertRequest doesn't provide the eventual key name, so when CertifiedKey is generated, the key name is set to a random string. When a key is not tied to a specific user, the key name is used to uniquely identify the key in the local attestation database. Thus, attestationd must set the name of the CertifiedKey in FinishCertRequest. BUG=chrome-os-partner:59478 TEST=Verify that the following succeeds: 1) attestation_client create_cert_request --profile=machine \ --origin=aaa --output=/tmp/cert_request 2) curl -X POST -v -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" \ -T /tmp/cert_request -o /tmp/cert_response \ https://chromeos-ca.gstatic.com/sign 3) attestation_client finish_cert_request --label=zzz \ --input=/tmp/cert_response 4) attestation_client info --label=zzz Change-Id: I23763eab8a9f2d6cc4e50794119d2016485ecd1d Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/410403 Commit-Ready: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Tested-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Benson Leung <bleung@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org>
